headline: Bangladeshi youth killed in BSF firing along Moulvibazar border
summary: A 20-year-old man was shot dead by the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) after allegedly entering Indian territory to smuggle goods.
details: A 20-year-old Bangladeshi youth, identified as Md. Mujib Ali, was killed on Friday evening in the Dattagram border area of Kulaura upazila in Moulvibazar.
According to Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), a group of six to seven Bangladeshi smugglers, assisted by Indian smugglers, illegally entered Indian territory around 7:00 pm to bring in smuggled goods.
Lt Col Sarkar Asif Mahmud, commanding officer of BGB Battalion-46, stated that BSF personnel from the Lathiapura camp intercepted the group.
The BSF claimed that the smugglers attempted to attack their personnel with locally made weapons, prompting the BSF to fire two to three rounds in self-defence.
Mujib Ali was killed on the spot, while the other members of the group fled back to Bangladesh and remain in hiding.
The BSF reportedly took the body away after the incident. Kulaura Police have also been dispatched to the scene to investigate.
caption:
A 20-year-old Bangladeshi man has been shot dead by the BSF at the Moulvibazar border.

A 20-year-old Bangladeshi youth, identified as Md. Mujib Ali, was killed on Friday evening in the Dattagram border area of Kulaura upazila in Moulvibazar.

According to Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), a group of six to seven Bangladeshi smugglers, assisted by Indian smugglers, illegally entered Indian territory around 7:00 pm to bring in smuggled goods.

Lt Col Sarkar Asif Mahmud, commanding officer of BGB Battalion-46, stated that BSF personnel from the Lathiapura camp intercepted the group.

The BSF claimed that the smugglers attempted to attack their personnel with locally made weapons, prompting the BSF to fire two to three rounds in self-defence.

Mujib Ali was killed on the spot, while the other members of the group fled back to Bangladesh and remain in hiding.

The BSF reportedly took the body away after the incident. Kulaura Police have also been dispatched to the scene to investigate.

headline: 79 people, including Bangladeshis, detained in Malaysia raid
summary: Malaysian authorities conducted an operation resulting in the arrest of 79 individuals, including citizens of Bangladesh.
details: Malaysian authorities carried out a targeted raid, resulting in the detainees being taken into custody.
A total of 79 people were detained during the operation, with Bangladeshi nationals among those arrested.
The operation was part of a broader effort by the authorities to enforce local laws and regulations.
Further details regarding the specific charges or the nature of the raid are yet to be fully disclosed.
